name: Communication Loss and the Fault Latch
description: The strongest of the five. A device stops answering; SafetyKernel only reacts after three consecutive missed cycles (a deliberate tolerance for one lost packet, not a bug) - watch that delay play out for real. Commands get blocked, then communication returns and the underlying condition clears, but the fault LATCH stays set: only a manual acknowledgement on the Alarms page clears it.

steps.description: The Modbus device stops answering. Nothing visibly reacts yet - SafetyKernel checks health once a second and only calls a device unhealthy after 3 consecutive missed cycles, deliberately tolerating one lost packet.

By now SafetyKernel has genuinely detected the loss (Safety.Modbus.Healthy went false, an alarm was raised, and new commands to this device were blocked) - see the Alarms page. Communication resumes here.

Safety.Modbus.Healthy is back to true within the next health-check cycle - but Safety.Modbus.Fault (the latch) stays set. This scenario deliberately does not acknowledge it: only a manual acknowledgement of the DEVICE_HEALTH_Modbus alarm on the Alarms page clears it, and Presentation Mode never does that for you (nor does stopping the presentation - the latch is real system state, not demo data). That's the entire point of this scenario - show it live from the Alarms page whenever you're ready.
